name: RealLit
description: RealLit: A Demographic-Aware Benchmark for Modeling Early Literacy Outcomes. The benchmark studies four cohorts. Three are distributed here as per-cohort CSVs: D2 (kindergarten screening cohort, n=1,039; D2/D2.csv, D2/D2_raw.csv), D3 (Florida district operational records; Grade 1-2 panel n=2,088 in D3/D3_G12.csv and D3/D3_G12_raw.csv, Grade 3 ELA cohort n=1,137 in D3/D3_G3.csv and D3/D3_G3_raw.csv), and D4 (longitudinal Grade 1-4 cohort, n=318; D4/D4.csv, D4/D4_raw.csv). D1 (ECRI benchmark) is loaded from its original public release and is not redistributed here.
citeAs: Anonymous Author. RealLit: A Demographic-Aware Benchmark for Modeling Early Literacy Outcomes.
rai:dataLimitations: D2: single-site U.S. metropolitan-area Kindergarten cohort (n=1,039); demographic fields come from a voluntary parent survey with 47-50% non-response; the Fall cognitive battery follows a non-overlapping sub-sample design (204 received all three subtests, 312 received one subtest only, 523 received none). End-of-Year follow-up coverage: NWD 49.6%, LWR 49.5%, CELF-5 SC 19.7%, CELF-5 RS 47.0%. D3: operational records from a single Florida district. The Grade 1-2 panel (n=2,088 across 14 schools; Grade 1 n=1,070, Grade 2 n=1,018) has 14.6% mean column missingness and derived-target coverage of 98.9% (below_level_3_fast) and 98.0% (below_grade_iready). The Grade 3 ELA cohort (n=1,137) has 1.9% mean column missingness with per-column gaps up to 9.1% (prior-year scale score), and carries no gender, race or ethnicity fields at all, so demographic analysis on D3 is limited to the Grade 1-2 panel. The Grade 3 Index column is a 1-1,137 row counter rather than a student key and does not link to the Grade 1-2 panel's CODED_ID, so the two D3 sub-cohorts cannot be joined at the student level. D4: single-site G1->G4 panel with grade-to-grade attrition (n=318 -> 298 -> 285 -> 220); per-grade mean column missingness rises from 3.9% (G1) to 36.5% (G4); per-form Word-Use Repertoire and SAT-10 percentile have lower coverage even within completed grades. Each cohort was administered a different assessment battery and is distributed as its own per-cohort file; missingness arising from a cohort's sub-battery or panel design is structural and should be masked, not modeled as MCAR/MAR.
rai:dataBiases: D2: single-site enrolment; race composition (per voluntary parent survey): white 28.6%, black 15.4%, multi-racial 5.8%, hispanic 4.9%, asian 1.4%; ~48% missing demographic data; cognitive battery administered only in cohort year 1 (correlated with year). D3: a single Florida district, 14 schools of 8-221 students each. Grade 1-2 panel composition: white 41.3%, hispanic 31.4%, black or african american 18.3%, other 7.0%, asian 1.8%, american indian or alaskan native 0.1%, native hawaiian or other pacific islander 0.0%; gender 53.7% male / 46.3% female; 13.5% English learners, 19.9% ESE, 5.6% Section 504 eligible, 3.4% gifted, 68.1% eligible for free or reduced-price lunch, 4.7% carrying a homeless-status code; primary home language is English for 79.1% and Spanish for 18.0%, with 13 further languages at 15 students or fewer. The Grade 3 cohort reports only ED (68.0%), ESE (19.2%), Section 504 (9.9%) and ELL (8.2%) and no race, ethnicity or gender, so it cannot support race- or gender-disaggregated analysis. Because D3 is district operational data, its ESE, Section 504, gifted and English-learner rates record administrative identification practice rather than underlying prevalence, and models fit to them will reproduce that practice. D4: single-site enrolment cohort entering G1 in 2007-08; race composition: white 59.4%, black 24.5%, mixed/multiple 6.0%, hispanic 4.4%, asian 3.8%; sex 51.3% male / 48.1% female. Demographic balance is fixed at intake and does not vary across grades.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: All three released cohorts ship de-identified student-level records containing no names and no dates of birth, and no free-text fields. D2 demographics are voluntary parent-survey responses (gender, ethnicity, race, language). D4 carries only Sex and Race at G1 intake. D3 is district operational data and carries more: the Grade 1-2 panel includes a surrogate student key (CODED_ID, unique per row) and a school identifier (SCHOOL_ID, 14 schools ranging from 8 to 221 students), alongside special-education (ESE), Section 504, gifted-eligibility, English-learner, primary home language, free/reduced-price lunch and homeless-status fields. These are administrative status categories rather than direct identifiers, but SCHOOL_ID combined with small school cells and low-frequency categories (home languages with fewer than 15 students; race categories at or below 0.1%) leaves a residual re-identification risk. Users must not attempt re-identification and should suppress or aggregate small cells before reporting. The Grade 3 cohort's Index column is a row counter, not a student key.
rai:dataUseCases: Early-reading risk prediction (D2 static at-risk indicator); longitudinal reading-recovery prediction (D4 G1 -> G3 spelling-score crossing); grade-level proficiency and grade-placement risk prediction from district operational records (D3 below_level_3_fast, below_grade_iready, below_level_2, below_level_3); tabular ML benchmarking under structured (MNAR) sub-battery and longitudinal-attrition missingness; demographic subgroup and fairness evaluation, for which the D3 Grade 1-2 panel carries the richest schema; cross-cohort generalization studies.
rai:dataSocialImpact: Released under CC BY 4.0; re-use permitted with attribution. D3 originates from a district data sharing agreement, and downstream users should confirm the district's terms before redistributing it. None of the cohorts is appropriate for individual student diagnostic, eligibility or placement decisions. D3's ESE, Section 504, gifted and English-learner fields record administrative classification decisions, so models trained on them can reproduce existing district identification patterns and must not be used to allocate or withhold services.
prov:wasDerivedFrom: Cohort 2: Kindergarten Fall battery and end-of-year follow-up assessments at a single U.S. metropolitan-area research site. Cohort 4: Single-site G1->G4 longitudinal study at the same research site.
prov:wasGeneratedBy: Each cohort ships as a pair of per-cohort CSVs in its own directory: a raw delivery (verbatim from the source) and a processed file byte-identical to it with derived target columns appended. D2 (D2/D2_raw.csv -> D2/D2.csv) adds 2 derived binary at-risk indicators (ktea3_nwd_target, ktea3_lwr_target) thresholded at standard score < 90. D4 (D4/D4_raw.csv -> D4/D4.csv) adds 1 derived binary recovery target (crossed_spell_target) thresholded on a G1 -> G3 spelling standard-score crossing of 100. D3 ships two sub-cohorts: the Grade 1-2 panel (D3/D3_G12_raw.csv -> D3/D3_G12.csv) adds a derived ELL indicator plus 2 derived binary at-risk targets (below_level_3_fast, below_grade_iready), and the Grade 3 ELA cohort (D3/D3_G3_raw.csv -> D3/D3_G3.csv) adds 2 derived binary at-risk targets (below_level_2, below_level_3). No aggregated cross-cohort file is distributed; the per-cohort CSVs are the primary artifacts.

field.name: ELL
field.description: Derived binary English-learner indicator: 1 if LEP_CODE is LY, LF or LA (currently or recently English-learner classified), else 0; no missing values.

field.name: below_grade_iready
